item.title: Everyone Blamed Her For The Crash | The Airbag Recorder Named The Only Driver Who Wasn't Belted
item.description:
The family swore she caused the crash that shattered her husband's spine, so why did the car's own recorder show the brake was never touched?
A collision analyst is blamed for the wreck that broke her husband's back, until the car's own crash recorder contradicts every person telling the story. The paperwork, the witness, and the family all agree. A chip the size of a matchbook does not.

item.title: They Said Her Father Was Too Confused To Sign | His Own Sensor Proved His Mind Was Clear
item.description:
They swore her father was too confused to know what he signed, so why did the sensor on his arm show a clear, steady mind at that exact hour?
After her father dies, his will is attacked as the work of a confused, failing mind. The doctor's note and the family agree he was slipping. But the small sensor on his arm had been quietly recording the truth of every hour, including the one when he signed.

item.title: She Flew to Vietnam to Buy Pearls Cheap. She Quit Her Job to Stop It Instead | A Relaxing Story
item.description:
Laura Kessler had flown to Vietnam to put her signature on a deal that would save her company nine dollars a pearl, and she was about to spend the next year making sure that signature never happened.
Laura Kessler spent fourteen years sourcing gemstones for a US jewelry chain. Her company sent her to Duong Dong, Phu Quoc, to lock in a cheap bulk pearl deal that would have rushed the harvest and ruined the oysters. She met the widow keeping the farm alive, saw exactly what the deal would do to it, and quit rather than sign it. A complete, relaxing story about walking away from a good job to help build a better one, on the real river town of Duong Dong, Phu Quoc, Vietnam. Names, characters, and the pearl farm are fictional.
